--- title: "Week 4: Discussion Section (`terra` and `stars`)" subtitle: "Practice raster manipulations" author: "Allie Caughmam, Alessandra Vidal Meza & Mary Salami" date: last-modified execute: message: false warning: false format: html: toc: true --- ::: {.callout-note icon=true} # Source Materials The following materials are modified from *Geocomputation with R* by Robin Lovelace. This page works through the same raster exercises twice: first with `terra` (Part 1), then with `sf` and `stars` (Part 2). ::: ## Get Started - Create a version-controlled R Project - Create a Quarto document ::: {.callout-warning} If you don't have `spDataLarge` installed, make sure to run:
`install.packages('spDataLarge', repos='https://nowosad.github.io/drat/', type='source')` ::: Let's load all necessary packages: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(spDataLarge) library(sf) library(stars) library(terra) ``` ::: You will be working with the following datasets: - Digital elevation model (DEM) of Mt. Mongón, Perú, obtained from `spDataLarge` - Landsat image of Zion National Park, obtained from `spDataLarge` - SRTM elevation of Zion National Park, obtained from `spDataLarge` ### Exercises 1. **Explore elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú** - Make a boxplot and histogram of elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú - Reclassify `dem` and compute the mean for the three classes: - Low, where elevation is less than 300 - Medium - High, where elevation is greater than 500 2. **Explore NDVI and NDWI at Zion National Park** - Calculate the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) at Zion National Park - Calculate the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) at Zion National Park - Find a correlation between NDVI and NDWI at Zion National Park 3. **Change resolution of elevation at Zion National Park** - Use all the methods available to change the resolution of elevation at Zion National Park to 0.01 by 0.01 degrees - **Note**: The `srtm` raster has a resolution of 0.00083 by 0.00083 degrees [Landsat 8 bands](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-8) 2-5 correspond to bands 1-4 for this raster. Bands are as follows: | Band | | Color | Resolution | | ---- | ----- | ---------- | | 1 | blue | 30 meter | | 2 | green | 30 meter | | 3 | red | 30 meter | | 4 | near-infrared | 30 meter | ::: {.callout-note icon=true} # Apply a scale factor and offset for all grid cells > Landsat Level-2 products are written as scaled integers to allow us to convert the data from floating point to integer for delivery. In most cases these are written to a 16-bit integer, which saves disk space and provides faster download times. Each floating point pixel has an offset applied and then multiplied by a gain to bring the value into the 16-bit integer (or unsigned integer) range. These values are referred to as scaled integers. To allow the user to get the data back to its original floating point value, a scale factor and offset are provided for each band. | Science product | Scale factor | Offset | | ---- | ----- | ---------- | | Surface reflectance | 0.0000275 | -0.2 | ::: First, correct the scale across all grid cells and then apply the following functions at each grid cell, in the image: $$\text{NDWI} = \frac{\text{(green - NIR)}}{\text{(green + NIR)}}$$ $$\text{NDVI} = \frac{\text{(NIR - red)}}{\text{(NIR + red)}}$$ ::: {.callout-important icon=true} Both parts use the same object names (`dem`, `landsat`, `srtm`, ...). Part 2 re-reads the data as `stars` objects, so it overwrites the `terra` objects from Part 1. Run the chunks in order. ::: # Part 1: `terra` ## 1. Load the data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dem <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/dem.tif", package = "spDataLarge")) landsat <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/landsat.tif", package = "spDataLarge")) srtm <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/srtm.tif", package = "spDataLarge")) ``` ::: ## 2. Explore elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Use terra:: so R doesn't fall back to base hist()/boxplot(), which can't read a SpatRaster terra::hist(dem, main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution", xlab = "Value") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} terra::boxplot(dem, main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution", ylab = "Value") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Define a reclassification matrix rcl <- matrix(c(-Inf, 300, 0, # values -Inf to 300 = 0 300, 500, 1, # values 300 to 500 = 1 500, Inf, 2), # values 500 to Inf = 2 ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE) # Apply the matrix to reclassify the raster, making all cells 0 or 1 or 2 dem_rcl <- terra::classify(dem, rcl = rcl) # Assign labels to the numerical categories # Old version: works with newer terra, but older versions (e.g., 1.7) error with # "[set.cats] the first column of 'value' must be numeric" because they don't accept a tibble # levels(dem_rcl) <- tibble::tibble(id = 0:2, # cats = c("low", "medium", "high")) # New version: a plain data.frame works with both older and newer terra levels(dem_rcl) <- data.frame(id = 0:2, cats = c("low", "medium", "high")) # Calculate mean elevation for each category using original DEM values elevation_mean <- terra::zonal(dem, dem_rcl, fun = "mean") elevation_mean ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` cats dem 1 low 274.3910 2 medium 392.0486 3 high 765.2197 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## 3. Explore NDVI and NDWI at Zion National Park - **Hint**: Explore the `terra` package to find a function that can help find the correlation! ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scale_factor <- 0.0000275 offset <- 0.2 scale_function <- function(x) { x * scale_factor + offset } landsat_scaled <- terra::app(landsat, fun = scale_function) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ndwi_fun <- function(green, nir){ (green - nir)/(green + nir) } ndvi_fun <- function(nir, red){ (nir - red)/(nir + red) } ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ndwi_rast <- terra::lapp(landsat_scaled[[c(2, 4)]], fun = ndwi_fun) ndvi_rast <- terra::lapp(landsat_scaled[[c(4, 3)]], fun = ndvi_fun) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(ndwi_rast, main = "Zion National Park NDWI") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(terra) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} combine <- c(ndvi_rast, ndwi_rast) # Stack rasters plot(combine, main = c("NDVI", "NDWI")) # Plot ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate correlation between raster layers terra::layerCor(combine, fun = cor) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [1,] 1.0000000 -0.9062336 [2,] -0.9062336 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## 4. Change resolution of elevation at Zion National Park ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(srtm) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rast_template <- terra::rast(terra::ext(srtm), res = 0.01) # Create empty template ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} srtm_resampl1 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "bilinear") srtm_resampl2 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "near") srtm_resampl3 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "cubic") srtm_resampl4 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "cubicspline") srtm_resampl5 <- terra::resample(srtm, y = rast_template, method = "lanczos") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} srtm_resampl_all <- c(srtm_resampl1, srtm_resampl2, srtm_resampl3, srtm_resampl4, srtm_resampl5) labs <- c("Bilinear", "Near", "Cubic", "Cubic Spline", "Lanczos") plot(srtm_resampl_all, main = labs) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: # Part 2: `sf` + `stars` ## 1. Load the data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dem <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/dem.tif", package = "spDataLarge")) landsat <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/landsat.tif", package = "spDataLarge")) srtm <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/srtm.tif", package = "spDataLarge")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} class(srtm) # should be "stars" in Part 2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "stars" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # A stars object is a list of arrays (attributes) plus a set of dimensions dem ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` stars object with 2 dimensions and 1 attribute attribute(s): Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max. dem.tif 238 366 478 555.9741 748 1094 dimension(s): from to offset delta refsys point x/y x 1 117 794599 30.85 WGS 84 / UTM zone 17S FALSE [x] y 1 117 8935384 -30.85 WGS 84 / UTM zone 17S FALSE [y] ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} landsat # Note the third dimension, "band" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` stars object with 3 dimensions and 1 attribute attribute(s), summary of first 1e+05 cells: Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max. landsat.tif 7701 8412 8739 8941.313 9258 14072 dimension(s): from to offset delta refsys point x/y x 1 1128 301905 30 WGS 84 / UTM zone 12N FALSE [x] y 1 1428 4154085 -30 WGS 84 / UTM zone 12N FALSE [y] band 1 4 NA NA NA NA ``` ::: ::: ## 2. Explore elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Extract the array of values from the first (and only) attribute dem_values <- as.vector(dem[[1]]) hist(dem_values, main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution", xlab = "Value") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} boxplot(dem_values, main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution", ylab = "Value") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Reclassify by cutting values into intervals, returning a factor raster dem_rcl <- cut(dem, breaks = c(-Inf, 300, 500, Inf), # -Inf to 300, 300 to 500, 500 to Inf labels = c("low", "medium", "high")) plot(dem_rcl, main = "Reclassified elevation") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate mean elevation for each category using original DEM values elevation_mean <- tibble(elevation = as.vector(dem[[1]]), cats = factor(as.vector(dem_rcl[[1]]), levels = levels(dem_rcl[[1]]))) %>% group_by(cats) %>% summarise(mean_elevation = mean(elevation, na.rm = TRUE)) elevation_mean ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 2 cats mean_elevation 1 low 274. 2 medium 392. 3 high 765. ``` ::: ::: Alternatively, we can use `sf` to turn the classes into polygons and then aggregate the original raster over those polygons: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Polygonize the reclassified raster, merging cells of the same class dem_polys <- sf::st_as_sf(dem_rcl, merge = TRUE) %>% group_by(dem.tif) %>% summarise() # Dissolve into one (multi)polygon per class # Compute the mean of DEM values falling inside each polygon aggregate(dem, by = dem_polys, FUN = mean) %>% sf::st_as_sf() %>% mutate(cats = dem_polys$dem.tif) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Simple feature collection with 3 features and 2 fields Geometry type: GEOMETRY Dimension: XY Bounding box: xmin: 794599.1 ymin: 8931775 xmax: 798208.6 ymax: 8935384 Projected CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 17S dem.tif geometry cats 1 274.3910 MULTIPOLYGON (((797252.2 89... low 2 392.0486 POLYGON ((797776.7 8934706,... medium 3 765.2197 POLYGON ((794599.1 8935384,... high ``` ::: ::: ::: ## 3. Explore NDVI and NDWI at Zion National Park - **Hint**: A `stars` attribute is just an R array, so base R functions work on it! ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scale_factor <- 0.0000275 offset <- 0.2 # Arithmetic on a stars object is applied to every grid cell landsat_scaled <- landsat * scale_factor + offset ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ndwi_fun <- function(green, nir){ (green - nir)/(green + nir) } ndvi_fun <- function(nir, red){ (nir - red)/(nir + red) } ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Split the "band" dimension into attributes (X1 = blue, X2 = green, X3 = red, X4 = NIR) landsat_bands <- split(landsat_scaled, "band") landsat_bands ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` stars object with 2 dimensions and 4 attributes attribute(s), summary of first 1e+05 cells: Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max. X1 0.4117775 0.431330 0.4403225 0.4458861 0.4545950 0.5869800 X2 0.3808675 0.424235 0.4372150 0.4434250 0.4559700 0.6300725 X3 0.3624975 0.408395 0.4303675 0.4419199 0.4632575 0.7378725 X4 0.3555675 0.618495 0.6523750 0.6498339 0.6853750 0.9389525 dimension(s): from to offset delta refsys point x/y x 1 1128 301905 30 WGS 84 / UTM zone 12N FALSE [x] y 1 1428 4154085 -30 WGS 84 / UTM zone 12N FALSE [y] ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ndwi_rast <- landsat_bands %>% transmute(ndwi = ndwi_fun(green = X2, nir = X4)) ndvi_rast <- landsat_bands %>% transmute(ndvi = ndvi_fun(nir = X4, red = X3)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(ndwi_rast, main = "Zion National Park NDWI") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot(ndvi_rast, main = "Zion National Park NDVI") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-26-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} combine <- c(ndvi_rast, ndwi_rast) # Combine as two attributes plot(merge(combine)) # Merge attributes into a dimension to plot side by side ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Calculate correlation between the two attributes cor(as.vector(combine$ndvi), as.vector(combine$ndwi), use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] -0.9062336 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## 4. Change resolution of elevation at Zion National Park ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=true} ## Solution ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(srtm) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-29-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create empty template from the bounding box of srtm rast_template <- stars::st_as_stars(sf::st_bbox(srtm), dx = 0.01, dy = 0.01) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # use_gdal = TRUE is needed for methods other than nearest neighbor srtm_resampl1 <- stars::st_warp(srtm, dest = rast_template, method = "bilinear", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999) srtm_resampl2 <- stars::st_warp(srtm, dest = rast_template, method = "near", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999) srtm_resampl3 <- stars::st_warp(srtm, dest = rast_template, method = "cubic", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999) srtm_resampl4 <- stars::st_warp(srtm, dest = rast_template, method = "cubicspline", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999) srtm_resampl5 <- stars::st_warp(srtm, dest = rast_template, method = "lanczos", use_gdal = TRUE, no_data_value = -9999) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} srtm_resampl_all <- c(srtm_resampl1, srtm_resampl2, srtm_resampl3, srtm_resampl4, srtm_resampl5) names(srtm_resampl_all) <- c("Bilinear", "Near", "Cubic", "Cubic Spline", "Lanczos") plot(merge(srtm_resampl_all)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week4-v2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-32-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: # `terra` vs. `stars`: what's the difference? ::: {.callout-note icon=true} # Source The written comparison below is based on [Chapter 7: Introduction to sf and stars](https://r-spatial.org/book/07-Introsf.html) in *Spatial Data Science: With Applications in R* by Edzer Pebesma and Roger Bivand. ::: Both packages gave the same answers above (identical class means and an NDVI–NDWI correlation of about -0.91). The difference is in how each package *represents* raster data. **`terra` (successor of `raster`)** - `raster`, and now its successor `terra`, has long been the main R package for powerful, flexible, and scalable raster analysis. - Its data model is a 2D regular raster, or a set (stack) of raster layers. This fits a static "GIS view" of the world, where each theme is a layer. - For data that change over time, a layer stack means the user has to keep track of which layer represents what (e.g., which layer is which date or band). **`stars` (spatiotemporal arrays)** - `stars` was written to support raster *and vector* data cubes. Raster layers, raster stacks, and feature time series are special cases of a data cube. - A `stars` object is a list of arrays (**attributes**) plus a table of **dimensions** (x, y, band, time, ...) with fields like `offset`, `delta`, and `refsys`. Time is just another dimension, so time-varying raster stacks are represented directly. - It handles regular grids as well as rotated, sheared, rectilinear, and curvilinear rasters, and arrays whose spatial dimension is a set of geometries (vector data cubes). - It is tightly integrated with `sf`: functions share the `st_` prefix, rasters can be cropped or aggregated with `sf` objects, and `st_as_sf()` converts back to `sf`. - It follows tidyverse design: `filter()`, `slice()`, `mutate()`, and `transmute()` work on data cubes. - It aims to scale beyond local disk size; `stars_proxy` objects are essentially pointers to files that are only read when needed. | | `terra` | `stars` | | --- | --- | --- | | **Data model** | 2D regular raster or a stack of layers | N-dimensional arrays (data cubes) with attributes and dimensions | | **Time-varying data** | User keeps track of which layer is which | Time is a dimension of the cube | | **Grid types** | Regular rasters | Regular, rotated, sheared, rectilinear, curvilinear, and vector data cubes | | **Scale** | Handles data up to the size of local storage | Aims beyond local disk size using `stars_proxy` objects | **How this showed up in this lab** | Task | `terra` (Part 1) | `stars` (Part 2) | | --- | --- | --- | | Multi-band data | Each band is a layer: `landsat_scaled[[c(4, 3)]]` | Bands are a dimension; `split()` turns them into attributes (`X1`–`X4`) and `merge()` reverses it | | Cell-wise math | `app()`, `lapp()` | Arithmetic is passed on to the arrays: `landsat * scale_factor + offset`, `transmute()` | | Reclassify and zonal statistics | `classify()` + `zonal()` | `cut()`, then `st_as_sf()` + `aggregate()` with polygons | | Resampling | `resample()` to a template | `st_warp()` to a target grid; the book recommends giving the target grid as a `stars` object, as we did with `rast_template` |
